title: SCH-CNT-002 weapon definition
description: A weapon definition. The project-owned typed validator in src/MechaMiner.Content/Categories/ remains authoritative; this schema is the draft 2020-12 mirror kept for editor and tool interoperability, and a fixture corpus proves the two reach the same accept/reject verdict on every structural case. See content/schemas/README.md. The recipe is two resource IDs and nothing else; one weapon file carried the same two materials four times. What the ID-only recipe costs is legibility, and the compensation is a relational check that resolves each recipe resource to its canonical letter and requires the concatenation to equal the weapon's own suffix.

id.title: A stable, case-sensitive ASCII content ID

recipe_pair_material_ids.description: The two resources this weapon is fabricated from, in authored order. The order is meaningful: the concatenation of the two resources' canonical letters, in this order, is the weapon ID's own suffix. The pair is unordered for uniqueness, which is why the catalog check sorts before comparing and this array does not.

minItems.derivation: a weapon ID is a two-letter material pair, so the recipe names exactly two resources; the floor is the length of the ID's suffix

maxItems.derivation: the same two as the floor, because the pair and the ID suffix have to line up character for character; a third material would have no letter to correspond to

signature_mech_id.description: The mech that deploys with this weapon.

behavior_kind.description: The registered behavior. A lower-kebab-case token. Whether it resolves to exactly one registered behavior descriptor is the behavior registry's check and is deliberately not asserted here.

targeting_policy.description: The registered targeting policy. A lower-kebab-case token. Whether it resolves to exactly one registered behavior descriptor is the behavior registry's check and is deliberately not asserted here.

rock_targeting_behavior.description: The registered rock-targeting behavior. A lower-kebab-case token. Whether it resolves to exactly one registered behavior descriptor is the behavior registry's check and is deliberately not asserted here.

ore_upgradeable_stats.description: The three ore-upgradeable stat tracks, in slot order. A branch may not add a fourth, so these three are the whole vocabulary a branch's effects can name.

minItems.derivation: the section states that the compiler verifies exactly three stats, so the floor is that number rather than an independent capacity choice

maxItems.derivation: the same three as the floor: 'exactly three' is one number, and a ceiling above it would admit a fourth stat that the compiler would then reject

fixed_properties.title: A registry-owned parameter map
fixed_properties.description: The weapon's fixed properties, keyed by its behavior kind. The key vocabulary belongs to the registered behavior descriptor rather than to this schema, so keys are not enumerated here; the strict codec still rejects a null, a duplicate key, and a non-snake_case key inside one.

global_attack_rate_mapping.title: The global attack rate mapping
global_attack_rate_mapping.description: Arrays of timing names rather than one sentence each, so a future validator can check that every listed timing is a timing the weapon has. The timing vocabulary is not closed: no accepted document enumerates one, and closing it from fifteen authored sentences would be inventing it.

affected_timings.description: The timings the global Attack Rate statistic reaches.

branch_ids.description: The three branch IDs, each beginning with this weapon's own ID. That they are one amplification, one functional and one conversion is asserted from the branches catalog, because branch_class lives on the branch.

minItems.derivation: the section states one amplification, functional and conversion branch per weapon, which is three; a weapon with two could not have one of each

maxItems.derivation: the same three as the floor; a fourth branch would be a second of one of the three kinds, and the section names each kind exactly once

base_automatic_attack_text.description: The one-sentence catalog description of the automatic attack. Kept because the weapon's behavior is not otherwise represented, and it is the strongest argument for the behavior registry existing.

version.title: A positive integer version
version.description: The initial schema_version and content_version of every first-authored definition is 1.

minimum.derivation: the initial value of every first-authored definition is 1 and both versions only ever increment, so no valid version is below 1; there is no upper bound because a definition may be revised without limit

name_key.title: Localization key for the player-facing name

summary_key.title: Localization key for the concise player-facing summary

tags.title: Closed query and tooling vocabulary
tags.description: The vocabulary starts empty, so [] is the only accepted value.

presentation_id.title: Logical presentation entry, required absent
presentation_id.description: Required absent: a definition carrying this field is an error. No accepted document says what a presentation definition contains, so no ID grammar has been minted for one, and minting a shape for a category with zero members would be inventing structure ahead of need. The field was declared-optional with a non-empty-string constraint, which accepted any string an author invented and validated nothing about it; rejecting the field outright fails loudly the first time somebody adds one instead of accepting an unauthorized value. The subschema is 'not' over the empty schema, which rejects every instance, so the fault is the field's presence rather than its shape and an authored empty string is rejected by the same rule rather than as an empty declared-optional field. The typed validator reports MMC-2010 and names the field. When an accepted document mints a presentation ID grammar, this declaration becomes that grammar; until then it has no minLength, because a length bound on a value that can never be authored explains nothing.

stat_track.title: An ore-upgradeable stat track
stat_track.description: One of a weapon's three tracks.

minimum.derivation: the section makes integer currency and rank values integral in source; a count of things that exist begins at one, because a count of zero is the absence of the field rather than a value of it

name.description: The track's name, which branch effects reference.

unit.description: The unit the two numeric values are measured in. The one place in the tree where a unit is a value rather than a name suffix, because rank_zero and increment_per_rank are a generic pair whose unit varies per row.

minimum.derivation: the section states that durations are nonnegative and that rates cannot be negative, so the floor of every duration and rate is zero and there is no upper bound the section supplies

increment_per_rank.description: What one common-ore rank adds. A track that does not improve with rank is not ore-upgradeable.

exclusiveMinimum.derivation: the section makes durations nonnegative and rates non-negative; this quantity is additionally one the definition divides by, scales by, or spends, so zero is excluded as well and the bound is exclusive rather than inclusive

discrete.description: Whether the value only takes whole steps.
